samples.summary: `COOKIE_SECURE=false` silently strips `Secure` **and** `__Host-` from every login and session cookie, including on an https origin, and is the one downgrade path the new warning does not cover
samples.evidence: `secureCookies` now returns the operator value first (github-auth.guard.ts:159-160) and `warnIfPlainHttpProduction` is reachable only from the derived `http://` branch (line 166-168). So `COOKIE_SECURE=false` on an https deployment makes `loginCookieName` emit the bare `wafflebase_oauth_state` / `wafflebase_cli_confirm` names (line 238) and `loginCookieOptions`/`baseCookieOptions` emit `secure:false` (line 249, auth.controller.ts:536) with nothing logged. The file's own comments (lines 222-232, 358-365) state that `__Host-` is the *only* control against an attacker planting the browser half of the double submit — a sibling subdomain (or an XSS on any host under the registrable domain) can then set `wafflebase_oauth_state`, harvest the matching `state` from one unauthenticated `GET /auth/github`, and complete a forced-login CSRF, and can also set the plain `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` cookies. A single misapplied env var (copied from a stale compose file, or set to fix a local dev loop and left in place) therefore turns off the change's central defence with no runtime signal at all, in a change whose stated contract is "the downgrade is configurable, and never silent" (auth.controller.ts:527-533).

samples.summary: `COOKIE_SECURE=true` now opens the `cliLoginAvailable` https gate on a genuinely plain-http, non-loopback deployment — the gate no longer reflects the origin's real scheme
samples.evidence: `cliLoginAvailable` (line 215-217) is `secureCookies() || loopbackCallback()`, and `secureCookies` now short-circuits on `COOKIE_SECURE` (line 159-160). Before this delta the gate could only be true when the configured callback URL was https; now an operator who sets `COOKIE_SECURE=true` to 'harden' an intranet install that is actually served over plain http passes the check at github-auth.guard.ts:514 and the CLI flow starts on a cleartext origin — exactly the deployment lines 208-213 say must be refused because 'the authorization code and the token it buys cross the network in the clear there anyway'. An on-path attacker on that network can then read the consent/state cookies and the authorization code. Mitigating factor I could not fully discount: browsers reject `Secure` cookies set from a non-secure origin, so on mainstream browsers the consent click would never complete and the flow would stall rather than leak — hence low confidence, but the gate itself is now assertable by config rather than derived.

samples.summary: The session and refresh cookies still carry no `__Host-`/`__Secure-` prefix, so even with `secureCookies()===true` a sibling subdomain can plant `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` — the protection the new comment claims for 'a cookie worth stealing' covers only the `Secure` flag
samples.evidence: `baseCookieOptions` (auth.controller.ts:534-538) returns `{httpOnly, secure, sameSite}` and `setAuthCookies` writes the fixed names `wafflebase_session` / `wafflebase_refresh` (lines 59-60, 484, 492) with no prefix and no `path`. Grep for `__Host-` across packages shows the prefix is applied only in `loginCookieName` (github-auth.guard.ts:238); no session cookie ever gets it. The guard's own reasoning (github-auth.guard.ts:222-232) is that without the prefix any sibling subdomain or anything able to inject a `Set-Cookie` for the registrable domain can write the cookie — applied to the session cookie that is session fixation: an attacker plants their own valid access/refresh token, the victim's browser sends it on every request, and the victim's work lands in the attacker's account. This delta's new comment (lines 527-533) asserts the session cookie's exposure is now handled by `COOKIE_SECURE` + the warning, which addresses only the transport flag, not cookie planting. Pre-existing code, raised because the delta reasons explicitly about this cookie's threat model.

samples.summary: An unrecognised `COOKIE_SECURE` value (`yes`, `on`, `TRUE!`, a typo) is silently discarded and the derivation takes over, so an operator who intended to assert https gets `Secure` dropped without knowing the setting was ignored
samples.evidence: `configuredSecureCookies` accepts only `true|1|false|0` and returns `undefined` for anything else (github-auth.guard.ts:83-89), and the caller falls straight through to the URL derivation (line 160-170). There is no env validation schema in the backend (grep for `validationSchema`/`validate:` in packages/backend/src returns nothing), so `COOKIE_SECURE=yes` on a TLS-fronted deployment whose callback URL still says `http://` yields `secure:false` on the session cookie with only the generic http warning — which names `COOKIE_SECURE=true` as the fix the operator believes they already applied. Rejecting or logging an unparseable value would make the misconfiguration visible.

samples.summary: The 'never silent' downgrade warning is gated on `NODE_ENV === 'production'`, so a real deployment started without that variable (and any deployment that sets `COOKIE_SECURE=false`) drops `Secure`/`__Host-` with no log at all
samples.evidence: `warnIfPlainHttpProduction` returns early unless `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` (github-auth.guard.ts:107-109) and is called from a single site, the derived `http://` branch (line 167). Only the shipped Dockerfile sets `NODE_ENV=production` (Dockerfile:88); a bare-metal `node dist/main.js` or a `pnpm start` behind a proxy does not, so the most likely misconfigured install — public domain, stale `http://` callback URL, no NODE_ENV — is exactly the one that gets no warning. The explicit `COOKIE_SECURE=false` path (line 160) returns before the warning site entirely. The claim in the doc comment and in auth.controller.ts:533 that the downgrade is 'never silent' therefore does not hold for two of the three ways it can happen.
searchedFor: read warnIfPlainHttpProduction and its only call site

samples.summary: The attacker-controlled `?error=` query value indexes `ERROR_MESSAGES` without an own-property check, so `/login?error=__proto__` resolves to `Object.prototype` and React throws while rendering — a crafted link that blanks the login page
samples.evidence: `const error = searchParams.get("error")` (login-form.tsx:28) is used directly as `ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR` (line 48) on a plain object literal typed `Record<string, string>` (line 13). `error=__proto__` returns `Object.prototype` (an object) and React refuses to render it ('Objects are not valid as a React child'), unmounting the tree; `error=toString`/`error=constructor` return functions. The result is a denial of the sign-in page from a link alone. The new test file added in this delta (packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/login-form.test.tsx) exercises only `login_state` and `something_new`, so nothing covers the prototype keys. `Object.hasOwn(ERROR_MESSAGES, error)` or a `Map` closes it.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the reviewer describes — `secureCookies` returns the operator value first (github-auth.guard.ts:159-160) and `warnIfPlainHttpProduction` is reachable only from the derived `http://` branch (166-168), so `COOKIE_SECURE=false` drops `Secure` and `__Host-` (238, 249, auth.controller.ts:536) with nothing logged. It is nonetheless not blocking under the security rubric: `COOKIE_SECURE` is an explicit, documented operator opt-out whose false-branch semantics are stated in the code itself (github-auth.guard.ts:67-89) and in operator docs (packages/backend/README.md:39-51, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:133-139). No attacker-controlled or request-borne input reaches it; the precondition is a deployer deliberately declaring an https origin to be plain http, which is the same class as choosing to serve cleartext. A repo-wide grep for `COOKIE_SECURE` finds only docs, the guard, the controller comment and the spec — no compose file, .env.example, Dockerfile or chart ships a `false` default, so the "stale compose file" premise has no instance in this tree. Every consumer of the predicate (loginCookieName 234-239, loginCookieOptions 246-253, cliLoginAvailable 215-217, baseCookieOptions 515-539) reads the same value, so there is no set/check asymmetry and no gate that is bypassed, inverted, or moved off the enforced path. The requested remedy is an extra warning log on an intentional documented downgrade, i.e. hardening/observability (minor on this rubric), not a critical/major security weakness.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists (secureCookies short-circuits on COOKIE_SECURE at github-auth.guard.ts:158-160; cliLoginAvailable at 215-217 gates line 514), but the claimed impact is unreachable. The same predicate that opens the gate also forces the login cookies to Secure/__Host- (loginCookieName:238, loginCookieOptions:249), so on the posited plain-http non-loopback origin the consent cookie cannot be stored by the browser (Secure from a non-secure origin, and __Host- requires Secure) — nor planted by an on-path attacker for the same reason. matchedConfirmation (607-622) reads the confirmation only from that cookie (618) and returns undefined without it, so canActivate re-renders the interstitial and returns at 569; the CLI state creation and redirect to GitHub (573-580, 591) are never reached. cliAuthStore.createState has exactly one production call site (573) — all other grep hits are specs — so there is no alternate unguarded entry. The result is a stalled login (a correctness/config issue), not the claimed leak of consent/state cookies or the authorization code. Additionally, the finding's premise that the gate previously 'reflected the origin's real scheme' is a counterexample: it was always config-derived — line 165 returns true from a configured https:// string and line 170 returns true for NODE_ENV=production with no callback URL at all, both possible on a plain-http box, and the comment at 127-132 says the live request scheme is deliberately not consulted. The residual is a trusted-operator misconfiguration with no attacker-controlled input.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: session cookies are written under the bare literals ACCESS_COOKIE_NAME='wafflebase_session'/REFRESH_COOKIE_NAME='wafflebase_refresh' (auth.controller.ts:59-60) at setAuthCookies (484,492) and clearAuthCookies (475-476), with baseCookieOptions (534-538) supplying only {httpOnly, secure, sameSite} — no name prefix and no path. The prefix helper loginCookieName (github-auth.guard.ts:234-239) is the sole application site of __Host- in the repo and is imported into this very controller, but used only for the CLI/login state cookie at auth.controller.ts:362, never for the session pair; other uses are guard lines 618/653/675 (state/confirm cookies). The read path confirms no prefixed variant exists: jwt.strategy.ts:13 reads request.cookies.wafflebase_session only. The project's own design doc corroborates the gap (backend.md:382-384 lists the session/refresh cookies without a prefix while wafflebase_oauth_state is __Host--prefixed). The guard's own comment (github-auth.guard.ts:222-232) states that without __Host- a sibling subdomain or a Set-Cookie injection for the registrable domain can write the cookie — applied to the session token this is session fixation, and no compensating control (path scoping, double-submit, session binding) exists. In-lane for the security rubric and major impact; the delta's new comment (527-533) addresses only the Secure transport flag.

finding.summary: Session/refresh cookie `Secure` flag is now derived from `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`'s scheme, so a misconfigured `http://` callback on a TLS-fronted deployment silently drops `Secure` from the session token
finding.evidence: `baseCookieOptions()` changed from `secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` to `secure: secureCookies(this.configService)` (auth.controller.ts:528). `secureCookies` (github-auth.guard.ts:91-98) returns `false` for *any* `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` starting with `http://`, and that branch is checked before the `NODE_ENV==='production'` fallback. Previously a production deployment always got `Secure` session/refresh cookies regardless of that variable. Now a deployment that terminates TLS at a proxy and leaves `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://...` (the exact spelling the self-hosting guide prints, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:121) serves `wafflebase_session` / `wafflebase_refresh` without `Secure` on an https site — the JWT then rides any plaintext request to the origin and is trivially stolen by a network attacker or a downgrade link. The reasoning in the comment (a Secure cookie on an http origin is dropped) is sound for a genuinely-http origin, but the predicate reads a config string, not the actual serving scheme, so one wrong env value silently removes a transport control from the session cookie rather than only from the 5-minute login cookie. Consider keeping `secure: true` whenever `NODE_ENV==='production'` OR the callback is https, and only relaxing for loopback.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is present in the tree: auth.controller.ts:534-538 sets the session/refresh cookies' `secure` flag from `secureCookies(this.configService)`, and github-auth.guard.ts:162-170 returns `false` for any `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` beginning with `http://`, checked before the `NODE_ENV === 'production'` fallback. A TLS-fronted deployment that leaves the callback URL as `http://` — the spelling the self-hosting guide prints at self-hosting.md:121 — therefore serves `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` without `Secure` on an https origin, which is an in-lane sensitive-data/transport-control weakness on a JWT session token. The finding's evidence is partly inaccurate: its line numbers are stale, and `secureCookies` actually consults an explicit `COOKIE_SECURE` override first (github-auth.guard.ts:80-89, 159-160) and emits a warning on the derived-false path under production on a non-loopback origin (github-auth.guard.ts:106-117), documented at self-hosting.md:133-139 — so the downgrade is not "silent". But an opt-in env override and a log line are not a guard that makes the unsafe path unreachable; with `COOKIE_SECURE` unset (the default) the downgrade still occurs. No named refutation ground applies, so the finding stays; confidence is low only because the documented override and warning make its blocking weight debatable, not its existence.
